# The Second Wave of Answers

date: 2026-11-24

> The author's answers to the refined checklist in `04`. Some questions are closed, others replaced by a clarification. The main point is the hard filter by role type (section 7).

## 1. Role: no direct choice, but a principle

Author: loves computers and technology, computer science and everything connected with it; mathematics, biology, chemistry and the other disciplines are appealing too.

Conclusion: this confirms the T-profile from `01`, rather than choosing a role. The vertical is CS/engineering, the horizontal is the natural sciences. So the role is chosen not by asking "what do I like more" (everything is liked), but by where the repository's artifacts meet demand. Working hypothesis: frontend/full-stack JS as the vertical, DevOps/platform as the second pillar, Web Audio/media as the amplifier.

## 2. What "commercial experience" means

The author does not understand the distinction. Clarification: commercial means paid employment; non-commercial means volunteering or unpaid help. There is no volunteer experience, but there is paid experience (the previously recorded 2 years). For the résumé we write jobs and projects; we skip the social experience section.

## 3. Geography

A direct transfer (L-1) is not available right away. The author is studying the routes carefully. It needs to be clarified in one word: remote work from Russia, or study as a bridge (F-1 → OPT → H-1B)?

## 4. Money and property

The author does not want to end up without property and admits to not knowing the real prices in every state and region: each has its own cost of living and culture. The threshold is therefore calculated not from a salary range but from the price of a house with land and the cost of keeping animals in a particular region. This is the subtractable "C" in the formula from `10`.

## 5. English

To prove the level, the author suggests the TOEFL. Distinction: TOEFL/IELTS are needed for study (F-1) and some visas; for hiring, a short conversation and a writing sample matter more. The test result, if it appears, is added to the hub as an artifact.

## 6. Education

It will be linked to the repository in the near future. No separate request is needed: education becomes another artifact of the hub.

## 7. Hard filter: an internal role, not a client-facing one

What does not suit the author: working with random people outside the company, being outside the corporate structure, maintaining a constant dialogue with external clients, "putting on a happy face". What suits: starting from internal interest; attracting a client with a real product and process; a role where you can speak plainly — where things are great and where they are not.

Conclusion: exclude freelancing, consulting, agencies, contract development, client-facing/support/sales. Keep an internal product or platform role within a company. This also explains why an honest README with a baseline of `23 PASS / 14 FAIL` is not a weakness but a filter for engineering culture.

Visa consequence: O-1 through an agent (typical for freelancers) does not suit the temperament; H-1B and L-1 with an employer are closer; EB-2 NIW is one's own endeavor without client service, but also without being "part of someone else's company".

## 8. Repository and links

The repository is already open and gradually developing — a correction to `09`, where the missing link was interpreted as a privacy issue. The problem is not access but a missing edge: there is no link to the repository in `/links/`. The other links are not being analysed yet: we need to understand what to extract from them.

## What remains open

- A region or state for calculating the price of a house with land.
- Confirmation or refutation of the role hypothesis from section 1.

Everything else is settled.
